newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ZEW IPO fully underwritten.
newsitem.headline: Polish ZEW IPO fully underwritten.

text.p: Societe Generale has underwritten 700,000 shares and Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) No.9 100,000 shares in the initial public offering of electrode maker ZEW SA, the fund said in a Friday statement.
The stand-by fee is three percent, the statement said.
ZEW, whose full name is Zaklady Elektrod Weglowych SA, is offering the public 800,000 shares from February 10 to February 18 at a minimum price of 38 zlotys.
The firm's main shareholders are NFI 9, with a 33-percent stake, and the state treasury, which has 25 percent.
ZEW's president Jerzy Szpineter told a news conference on Friday that the firm expected to lift net profit to about six million zlotys this year from 1996's 1.3 million zlotys.

He said 1996's planned net of 5.3 million zlotys was cut by the recent ruling requiring former state-owned companies to recalculate depreciation for 1995 and the first nine months of 1996 based on gross value of assets rather than net value.
ZEW had 153.9 million zlotys in sales last year. Fund officials on Friday said the firm should record sales of 190-200 million zlotys this year.
